extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the ARPA-E OPEN 2021 FOA (universities, national labs, startups, small & large businesses, federal labs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and FAQ rules for preparing and submitting Concept Papers and Full Applications to the ARPA‑E OPEN 2021 funding opportunity, including eligibility, cost share, formatting, teaming, and intellectual property/manufacturing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial partner requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Do we need to have an industrial partner in the application to OPEN2021?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer: No. An industrial partner is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: No ARPA‑E pre‑assessment / no teaming guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E will not pre‑assess an applicant’s proposal or provide teaming arrangement guidance to potential applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants must independently review the FOA technical requirements and determine whether their proposed concept warrants submission; ARPA‑E will not evaluate drafts or advise on teaming prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E is not limiting the number of submissions from Applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may submit more than one application to this FOA, provided that each application is scientifically distinct (per FOA Section III.C.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept paper single concept requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Concept Paper must be limited to a single concept or technology; unrelated concepts and technologies must not be consolidated into a single Concept Paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission uses multiple approaches to pursue one concept, applicants should judge whether the approaches constitute a single concept; ARPA‑E will not pre‑assess whether the submission is compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of performance maximum
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of performance for funding agreements may not exceed 36 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See FOA Section II.A for details on period of performance and other schedule constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI must meet all eligibility requirements for applicants as stated in the FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must consult FOA Section III. Eligibility Information to confirm PI and institutional eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full application budget documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must complete all budget information in section D. Content and Form of Full Applications 3. THIRD COMPONENT: BUDGET JUSTIFICATION WORKBOOK/SF-424A of the FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete budget justification and SF-424A must be submitted with the full application; estimated totals in the concept paper are not the only budget information ultimately required.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR and small business participation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no SBIR-specific portion of the OPEN 2021 solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses may apply to the OPEN 2021 FOA (but this is not an SBIR set‑aside).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign work / foreign collaborator waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: All project work must be conducted in the U.S. unless a partial waiver is granted; foreign collaborators or foreign work generally require a foreign work waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver requests are submitted with the Business Assurances Form during the Full Applications phase and are negotiated case‑by‑case with selected applicants. Even partners providing only in‑kind cost share or no funds (e.g., co‑supervising students) may require a waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑US applicants / US subsidiary requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign entities are eligible to apply but must designate in the Full Application a subsidiary or affiliate incorporated (or to be formed) in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may submit concept papers as non‑US entities, but the U.S. subsidiary/affiliate must be fully incorporated prior to award; the ARPA‑E eXCHANGE system allows changes to the Project Team for the Full Application, but incorporation is required before award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperlinks allowed in concept paper PDFs
rubrics_metrics.description: Can a compliant concept paper include hyperlinks embedded in the text of the .pdf file to provide references?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yes — reviewers are able and allowed to click on embedded hyperlinks for expanded information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept paper color and figure policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Text within a concept paper must be black; use of color in photos, drawings, illustrations, or figures must follow FOA formatting standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must follow standards prescribed in FOA Section IV. Application and Submission Information C. CONTENT AND FORM OF CONCEPT PAPERS. Confirm whether reviewers will view in color per the FOA guidance and submission/printing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept paper formatting (margins, font, spacing)
rubrics_metrics.description: All pages must be formatted to fit on 8-1/2 by 11 inch paper with margins not less than one inch on every side. Single space all text and use Times New Roman typeface, a black font color, and a font size of 12 point or larger (except in figures and tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formatting requirement applies to all text in the concept paper including footnotes and references (references must use 12 point and count toward page limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept paper page limit and references
rubrics_metrics.description: References are assumed to be included in the 4 page concept paper limit and must use the required font/formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References may not be reduced to a 10 point font to evade formatting rules; follow FOA IV.C content and form rules and the explicit statement that font size requirement applies to footnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept paper file naming / upload
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the Concept Paper file we upload to xCHANGE require a specific naming nomenclature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ARPA‑E Funding Opportunity Exchange website automatically renames files on upload to the submission record; applicants do not need to apply a particular file‑name convention for the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and documentation in concept paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Team Organization and Capabilities information required for concept paper submissions must follow FOA Section IV.C.d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple organizations are involved, the lead applicant should consult IV.C.d to determine what information/documentation about team members is needed for the concept paper and full application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Team modification between concept and full application
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARPA‑E eXCHANGE system will allow applicants to expand or otherwise modify the Project Team for their Full Applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable to list a place‑holder lead at concept stage and add/adjust team members for the full application, but applicants must ensure full‑application compliance and final team incorporation/eligibility prior to award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lab facilities requirement and legal representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do lab facilities need to be in place (i.e. leased) by my start‑up before, during or after award negotiations? What legal representations need to be made?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lab facilities need to be in place prior to award negotiations. Applicants are responsible for determining and making any legal representations regarding lab facilities during award negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of companies on Project Team
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there any limitation for the number of companies (small or large businesses) that can be part of one concept paper as part of the Project Team?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No numerical limit, but Project Teams must meet all compliance criteria in the FOA (e.g., cost share, eligibility, IP rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost share: basic reduced requirements and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Teams composed exclusively of domestic educational institutions, domestic nonprofits, and/or FFRDCs/DOE Labs/Federal agencies (other than DOE) are required to provide at least 5% of the Total Project Cost as cost share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review FOA Section III.B.3 for full definitions and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost share: 10% reduction eligibility and large business carve‑out
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Teams where domestic educational institutions, domestic nonprofits, small businesses, and/or FFRDCs perform >=80% of the total work (by Total Project Cost) are required to provide at least 10% of the Total Project Cost as cost share. However, any entity (such as a large business) receiving patent rights under a class waiver, or other patent waiver, that is part of a Project Team receiving this reduction must continue to meet the statutory minimum cost share requirement (20%) for its portion of the Total Project Cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the FOA footnotes and definitions for 'For‑Profit Organization' and specific allocation calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost share grace period for small businesses / multi‑year projects
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient qualifies for the cost share grace period, the 10% cost share requirement becomes effective only if the project is not terminated during the first year. If the project continues beyond that time, the recipient will owe 10% of the total project cost, including the costs incurred during the grace period. If the project does not continue beyond one year, the recipient will not be required to contribute cost share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review the FOA Reduced Cost Share section closely for eligibility and implications when planning multi‑year efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable cost‑share items (data, personnel, in‑kind)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data under certain circumstances may be an allowable cost‑share. Personnel costs can be an allowable in‑kind contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See FOA Cost Sharing sections and General FAQ 4.14 for examples and valuation methodology; value of in‑kind contributions (e.g., datasets) may require justification and may be evaluated/negotiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Startup incorporation requirement and review preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Does a start‑up need to be incorporated before concept submission or award?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet criteria in FOA Section III. Eligibility Information A. Eligible Applicants. The lead entity must be incorporated prior to award (the U.S. subsidiary must be fully incorporated prior to award). No preference is given to already‑incorporated applicants during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement policy parity
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E’s policy for reimbursement of expenses treats all awardees equally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no ARPA‑E policy to provide upfront portions of award uniquely to small businesses; applicants must plan for reimbursements and cash flow accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property / subject invention manufacturing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject Inventions — and related patents — arising from ARPA‑E research projects must be manufactured/used for manufacture in the U.S. (including U.S. territories) for sales anywhere in the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected Applicants/Awardees may request partial waivers to allow some non‑U.S. manufacturing when justified for economic reasons and with offsetting U.S. benefits; waivers are negotiated during the Full Application/Business Assurances phase. See FOA Sec. VIII. 'Other Information A. Title to Subject Inventions' for obligations that continue after project completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions requiring FOA section cross‑reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Several FAQ answers direct applicants to specific FOA sections (e.g., IV.C Content & Form of Concept Papers; III.B.3 Cost Sharing; Section II.A period of performance; Section VIII IPR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the cited FOA sections for authoritative, detailed rules and use the FAQs as clarifications only. ARPA‑E will correct typographical errors via modification where indicated.
